title: Printed dates and times use the server's time zone (UTC), not the shop's: evening check-ins and payments show the next day on invoices; repair history and 'commission this month' are shifted too
description: Round 1 added Shop.timeZone and used it for 'taken today' and the sales range. fmtDate still calls toLocaleDateString('en-US') without a timeZone, so on the hosted (UTC) server every date it renders is a UTC date: the invoice 'Received'/'Returned'/'Paid <date>'/warranty 'through', and the ticket, invoice and machine lists. The sewing shop's repair History uses `new Date(e.at).toLocaleString("en-US")` (repairs/[id]/page.tsx:164) in UTC. The repairs page's 'commission earned this month' boundary is `new Date(y, m, 1)` in server time (repairs/page.tsx:27) rather than monthRange(tz). The Checklist client component renders `new Date(s.at).toLocaleString()`, which differs between server and browser, so every ticket page with a ticked item throws a React #418 hydration error and re-renders on the client.
failure_scenario: A shop in America/New_York checks a machine in at 9:30 pm on Sep 24 and the customer pays at 10:15 pm on Sep 25. The printed invoice says 'Received Sep 25, 2026' and 'Paid Sep 26, 2026 (Card)'. On the last evening of a month after 8 pm, /repairs already reports the next month's commission.
suggested_fix: Give fmtDate (and a fmtDateTime) a timeZone parameter and pass shop.timeZone from the pages; use `timeZone` in the Intl options. Use monthRange(tz) or startOfMonth(tz) on /repairs. In the Checklist, render the timestamp from a server-formatted string, or format it only after mount, to avoid the hydration mismatch.
evidence: Server TZ is UTC (`date` shows UTC; the next-server environ has no TZ). I set my own ticket's intakeAt to '2026-09-25 01:30Z' (Sep 24 21:30 EDT) and the payment's paidAt to '2026-09-26 02:15Z'. The invoice shows 'Received Sep 25, 2026 | ... | Paid Sep 26, 2026 (Card)'. s15.js on a ticket with a ticked checklist item: 'PAGEERROR Minified React error #418; ... args[]=text'. Code: format.ts:22-26 `x.toLocaleDateString("en-US", { month: "short", day: "numeric", year: "numeric" })`.
verifier_notes: confirmed: fmtDate (format.ts:22-26) calls toLocaleDateString('en-US') with no timeZone, so it uses the server zone (UTC on the hosted server). The invoice's Received, Returned, Paid and warranty dates and the list dates come from it. repairs/page.tsx:27 computes the start of the month with new Date(y, m, 1) in server time. The Checklist client component (ticket-controls.tsx:87) renders new Date(s.at).toLocaleString(), which differs between server and browser. Round 1 added Shop.timeZone but applied it only to day/month ranges, so the fix is incomplete. For western US shops, events after 5 pm local land on the next day, which is a real share of business hours. The desktop program runs in local time and is not affected.
also_reported_as: code: src/lib/format.ts:25 Invoices and ticket dates, and the repairs page's 'this month', use the server's time zone (UTC when hosted), not the shop's

title: Receipts, register sales times, sales log dates and the sales CSV use the server's time zone (UTC on hosted), not the shop's
description: Round 1 made the report ranges use the shop's zone (monthRange, todayIn), but the displayed dates and times are still formatted in the server's zone. Receipt time (line 42) and the void time (line 30) call toLocaleString without timeZone. So do the register sales list (register/sales/page.tsx:132), the sales-log header (sales/page.tsx:49; `end - 1ms` is the NEXT day in UTC for any US zone) and its payment dates (:122), the register-sales header (register/sales/page.tsx:49), and the price list 'Effective' date (price-list/page.tsx:49). The sales CSV date column is `p.paidAt.toISOString().slice(0,10)` (api/sales/route.ts:19), a UTC date, so an evening payment is filed under the next day, or the next month at month end.
failure_scenario: Hosted server (TZ=UTC), shop in America/New_York, 1:20 PM EDT. The printed receipt says '9/26/26, 5:20 PM'. /sales?from=2026-09-01&to=2026-09-25 shows the header 'Sep 1, 2026 to Sep 26, 2026'. A payment taken at 9 PM EDT on Sep 30 appears in the September CSV dated 2026-10-01.
suggested_fix: Pass the shop's zone everywhere a date is shown: add fmtDate(d, tz) and fmtDateTime(d, tz) helpers that set `timeZone`, select shop.timeZone on the receipt page (sale.shop is already loaded), and in /api/sales use `iso(zonedParts(p.paidAt, tz))` for the date column. For the range headers, format fromStr/toStr directly rather than instants.
evidence: Playwright: RECEIPT '9/26/26, 5:20 PM' while 'now NY 9/26/2026, 1:20:40 PM'; '/sales header: Sales log | Sep 1, 2026 to Sep 26, 2026' for to=2026-09-25; /register/sales rows '1004 Sep 26, 5:20 PM ...'. Server TZ: `node -e Intl...timeZone` -> UTC; no TZ in the next-server environment.
verifier_notes: confirmed: The dates shown are formatted in the server's zone: receipt createdAt (register/sales/[id]/page.tsx:42) and voidedAt (:30), the register sales list (register/sales/page.tsx:132), and fmtDate (format.ts:22-26, no timeZone), which the sales log header and payment rows use. The running next-server processes have no TZ set and resolve to UTC, which is also the hosted default (railway.json sets none). The sales log header formats `end - 1ms`, where end is the next shop-local midnight (04:00Z for New York), so it lands on the following UTC day. /api/sales dates rows with paidAt.toISOString().slice(0,10). paidAt is @default(now()), a real instant, so evening payments get the next UTC date while being included in the shop-zone range. On the Windows program the server runs in the shop's own zone, so this only affects the hosted app.
also_reported_as: qa: src/app/(app)/register/sales/[id]/page.tsx:42 Receipts, register reports and the sales log show times and dates in the server's time zone, not the shop's (round-1 time-zone fix incomplete)

title: Receipts, sales lists and the sales CSV use the server's clock (UTC on hosted), not the shop's time zone
description: Round 1 made report ranges start at the shop's midnight (monthRange/zonedMidnight), but the dates and times shown or exported for each row still use the server's local zone, which is UTC on Railway. /api/sales writes `p.paidAt.toISOString().slice(0, 10)`, the UTC date. The receipt (register/sales/[id]/page.tsx:42, and :30 for the void time), the register-sales Time column (register/sales/page.tsx:132) and the Sales log dates (sales/page.tsx:122, via fmtDate) all call toLocaleString/toLocaleDateString without timeZone. The page headers `fmtDate(start)` (register/sales/page.tsx:49, sales/page.tsx:49) show the day before for any shop east of UTC, because the shop's midnight is the previous day in UTC. The register-sales export also writes createdAt as a UTC ISO timestamp.
failure_scenario: A New York shop takes an $85 cash payment at 9:30 PM on Sep 25. GET /api/sales?from=2026-09-25&to=2026-09-25 correctly includes it, but its date column says 2026-09-26, so a month-end CSV lists next-month dates and spreadsheet totals by date don't match the page. A register sale at 1:11 PM EDT prints "9/26/26, 5:11 PM" on the customer's receipt, and after 8 PM EDT receipts show tomorrow's date.
suggested_fix: Pass the shop's timeZone to every date and time formatter on these pages (toLocaleString("en-US", { timeZone: shop.timeZone, ... })), for example by giving fmtDate a timeZone parameter. In /api/sales, write the date as todayIn-style zoned parts: iso(zonedParts(p.paidAt, tz)). Format the header dates from fromStr/toStr instead of from the instants.
evidence:
Server TZ: `node -e 'Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone'` -> UTC (same as hosted).
Payment inserted at 2026-09-26 01:30Z in own shop (tz America/New_York); t5.mjs output:
  date,ticket,customer,via_account,brand,model,serial,method,amount,note
  2026-09-26,51,José Núñez,,Janome,MC6700P,'=1+2,Cash,85.00,evening pickup
  (for from=2026-09-25&to=2026-09-25)
t6.mjs: sale 1001 createdAt 2026-09-26 17:11:58Z (13:11 EDT) -> receipt time: 9/26/26, 5:11 PM; list times: 'Sep 26, 5:12 PM', ...
verifier_notes: confirmed: Accurate. The /api/sales date column is `p.paidAt.toISOString().slice(0,10)` (route.ts:19), which is always the UTC date whatever time zone the server runs in. The receipt (register/sales/[id]/page.tsx:30 and :42), the register-sales Time column (register/sales/page.tsx:132) and fmtDate (format.ts:22-25) are server components that format without a timeZone, so they use the server zone. On Railway that is UTC: railway.json and INSTALL.md set no TZ, and the repo never sets process.env.TZ. Round 1 made the report ranges zone-aware (monthRange/zonedMidnight) but left display and export formatting out, so that fix is incomplete. Every register receipt and sales-list time on a hosted install is off by the UTC offset. Evening payments land on the next day in the CSV, and page headers show the previous day for shops east of UTC. The Windows program runs in local time and is not affected. No money totals are wrong; these are display and export dates on common hosted flows.
also_reported_as: qa: src/app/api/sales/route.ts:19 Repair-payments CSV dates each row with the UTC date, so evening payments land in the next day or month
